(WHDH) - The University of New Hampshire (UNH) is investigating a burglary at a dormitory building on campus early Saturday morning that occurred while the residents were asleep. On October 3, the University said an unknown man “unlawfully” entered the residents’ room in Stoke Hall and attempted to steal items while they were sleeping. The University said the incident happened between 2 and 2:15 a.m. Stoke Hall is the largest residence hall at UNH, located near the heart of campus. Some students said the crime has left them on edge. “It’s beyond words, like, if that happened to me, I don’t even know what I would do,” said Freddy Ciampa, a UNH student. “Just the thought of somebody breaking in while I’m asleep and taking my stuff, terrible.” In an email sent to students, the University is encouraging everyone to lock all doors and windows, ensure their locks are working, do not let unknown individuals into the building, and immediately report suspicious activity to UNH Police. “Not good; it’s very scary. Me and my roommate have now been keeping our doors locked. I know a lot of people have,” said Riley Need, a UNH student. “It’s been spreading all over campus and everyone’s scared, so we’re waiting for updates from the UNH Police Department.” 7NEWS has reached out to UNH police and the University; both said the incident remains under investigation. title: NH Farmers Star in Video Series About Produce Safety - University of New Hampshire
content: You’d think there’d be no one better prepared to provide safe produce than Forrest Barker, who was raised on a farm, attended university for agricultural science, and is now the fifth generation of her family to run Barker’s Farm in Stratham. Yet, even she found ways to improve her practices through the Jumpstart to Produce Safety program offered by UNH Extension starting in 2022. In fact, Barker was so appreciative that she agreed to film a series of short videos the produce safety practices she learned through the program. Those videos, which also feature other program participants, have resulted in something that Mary Choate, program organizer for Extension, didn’t even foresee from the outset: a trove of vignettes from growers explaining how best practices are implemented at their farm. Some of those implementations are surprising — did you know that a clothes dryer can be converted into a vegetable spinner? — but more often, the videos show how several small changes can add up to a significant lowering of food safety risks. The video series is the culmination of the four-year Jumpstart to Produce Safety program. Funded by the USDA and administered by UNH Extension and UMaine Extension, the program was intended to assist growers in moving toward compliance with the Food Safety Modernization Act and ensuing produce safety rules. Most New Hampshire farms are small enough that they aren’t required to follow FSMA rules, however, 28 growers from the Granite State signed up — and more from Maine — which indicates to Mary Choate, food safety specialist for UNH Extension, that their commitment to safety runs deeper than mere compliance. Over the program, participants gained an on-site food safety assessment, one-on-one guidance for writing a food safety plan, access to useful templates, and ongoing support with implementing the plan. Farmers found low- or no-cost ways to implement many of the upgrades, Choate says, and found benefits that went beyond safety. For example, moving the handwashing station to a convenient location both improves frequency of handwashing and reduces the time it takes to reach the sink. Worn-out harvest baskets are harder to keep clean and are also a pain to use. Installing triple-bay sinks allows for both better sanitation and a streamlined workflow. Lastly, produce that is properly cleaned has a longer shelf life and is more appealing to customers. As Jumpstart was drawing to a close, Choate said that she and other organizers wanted to document the program’s success as a way to share it further. “We had all these great changes by farmers. We thought, why don’t we take these farmers who will agree to be on video and micro-learning videos,” says Choate. “Farmers talking to farmers, peer learning.” More than 70 videos resulted — most between one and three minutes — each featuring a grower explaining, in their own words and on their own farm, how produce safety is integrated into their practices. On Barker’s Farm, Forrest Barker says there were a few small but significant changes, such as using pallets in the washroom to place produce containers on, instead of placing them directly on the concrete floor. She is also excited about the food-safe sanitizing spray and scrub brush she discovered through the program. But above all, Barker said the biggest improvement was the creation of a standard operating procedure document — a binder full of practices, many of which had existed in only her or her mother’s head. “It makes it easier to follow them better, but it’s also knowing that everyone knows,” Barker says. “It’s making sure that it’s common knowledge, and it’s not on me to make sure I’m teaching everyone everything they should be doing. I definitely feel more confident in the cleanliness of everything.” Copyright © 2026 , University of New Hampshire. All rights reserved.

title: Man Breaks Into UNH Dorm Room While Students Slept, Police Warn Campus - Hoodline
content: A man with brown hair slipped into a Stoke Hall dorm room at the University of New Hampshire early Sunday while students were asleep inside, and tried to make off with their belongings before campus police were called in. The break-in happened at about 2 a.m. in Durham, prompting UNH police to issue a warning urging students across campus to lock their doors and windows and report anything suspicious. According to WMUR, the investigation into the Stoke Hall incident remains ongoing, and officials have not released further detail on the suspect beyond his brown hair. Stoke Hall is the largest residence hall at UNH and sits near the heart of campus, according to the university's own housing office, making it one of the more heavily populated dorms where such a warning would reach a large number of students at once. This is not the first time UNH police have asked the campus community for help tracking down someone targeting dorm rooms. Officers have previously said they were working to track down a person behind a series of dorm burglaries, per the station's earlier reporting. In that case, police received three reports on Monday and Tuesday of burglaries happening at Handler Hall, another residence hall on campus. Those Handler Hall incidents, reported in March, were tied to a narrower kind of theft. The student newspaper notes that the only items that have been reported stolen are UGGs and other similar footwear, according to the The New Hampshire. In one of those cases, an unknown suspect entered a dorm room around 5:55 p.m. on March 2 and stole a pair of UGG slippers, prompting UNH police to issue a timely warning notification the following evening, at 7:10 p.m. on March 3, regarding the burglary investigation in Handler Hall. A fourth report from that same string of incidents described an unknown male who went into a room but left when the resident acknowledged him, the outlet's earlier coverage states. Sunday's incident is not the first time Stoke Hall has been the subject of an intruder warning. Back on September 10, 2004, students were warned to lock their dorm room doors after several reports of theft and intruder sightings, according to the Sun Journal. Those sightings and cash thefts had all happened at Stoke Hall, which was described at the time as a women's dormitory, and students said they saw a man leaving their rooms as they returned home. The 2004 suspect was described as 5-foot-9, in his 30s, with scraggly hair, and the hall's director at the time, Brian Williams, warned students not to let strangers into the building and to keep their valuables out of sight. For now, officials are urging the roughly 25 residence halls' worth of students across UNH's campus to keep their doors and windows locked and to report any suspicious activity they see. With the investigation into Sunday's break-in still active, police have not said whether any property was taken or whether the man has been identified. title: SA analyst upgrades/downgrades: NVDA, UNH, CLSK, CAT - TradingView
content: Recent analyst actions from Seeking Alpha feature upgrades for CleanSpark, Inc. CLSK and Caterpillar Inc. CAT, alongside downgrades for Nvidia Corporation NVDA and UnitedHealth Group UNH. Seeking Alpha analysts have shifted CleanSpark to Hold following a landmark AI infrastructure lease, while Caterpillar was upgraded to Buy ahead of earnings due to record Q2 growth. Conversely, Nvidia was downgraded to Hold on inventory turnover concerns, and UnitedHealth Group was downgraded to Sell as fundamental recovery appears fully priced in. Caterpillar CAT: Upgrade to Buy by Mike Zaccardi, CFA, CMT. The analyst views shares as undervalued relative to robust forward EPS growth, supported by record-breaking Q2 earnings, $20.5B in revenue (+23.5% YoY), and a $72.1B order backlog. "CAT continues to stay a step ahead of its peers and broader market demand through aggressive execution. Its focus is on mega projects in North American construction, and the industrial-AI firm is now rapidly expanding power and turbine capacity. Cost inflation remains a risk, but the business has been able to push along price hikes to combat what's going on with raw materials." CleanSpark CLSK: Upgrade to Hold by Gary Alexander. The analyst cites improved visibility following a landmark 20-year, $6.6B triple-net lease in Sandersville as the company transitions into AI infrastructure, though capital requirements and debt cost details remain key risks. "CleanSpark CLSK, in my view, is looking increasingly convincing. The Bitcoin mining stock is making major strides in diversifying itself as an AI infrastructure provider. Based on its first major deal signed in the space, CleanSpark has a fantastic opportunity to extend its expertise and secure its future beyond the volatility of crypto mining." Nvidia NVDA: Downgrade Buy to Hold by Envision Research. The downgrade reflects evolving catalysts post-FQ2 earnings, specifically inventory turnover slowing to a multi-year low of 3.35x alongside memory and substrate wafer supply constraints. "The upbeat growth is offset by both fundamental uncertainties (such as the slowed inventory turnover, memory and substrate wafer constraints, etc.). Combined with the technical signs, we see good odds of consolidation in the near term. These considerations were sufficiently materially for us to adjust our rating to hold." UnitedHealth Group UNH: Downgrade to Sell by Bears of Wall Street. The analyst notes that the risk/reward profile has flipped following a stock rebound from $300 to $440-$450, leaving little margin of safety amid persistent medical cost inflation and challenges in Commercial and Medicaid segments. "The market is already paying heavily for the successful turnaround, and, in our opinion, the most obvious part of recovery has already taken place. Also, the next stage will be more difficult and will require much better execution. As a result, we decided to change our rating from Buy to Sell." (CSX), Penguin Solutions (PENG) and UnitedHealth Group (UNH) stocks climbed to new 52-week highs on Thursday as investors channeled capital toward companies with durable business models and sector-specific growth drivers as the second-quarter (Q2) earnings season approaches. While CSX and UnitedHealth Group ended the session 1% higher each, Penguin Solutions ended the session up 3%. CSX stock reached a record high of $49.54 on Thursday as analysts became more constructive on the railroad operator's prospects. Citi increased its price target on CSX to $53 from $46 while leaving its ‘Neutral’ unchanged. The updated forecast comes as the firm expects transportation companies to deliver some of their best quarterly earnings in years, driven by favorable market conditions. According to Citi's analysis, tighter freight capacity across transportation networks has created a more supportive pricing environment for operators. At the same time, demand has gradually improved, providing an additional tailwind for companies across the sector as they prepare to report Q2 results. The company is set to report Q2 earnings on July 22, and analysts see $3.84 billion revenue with earnings of $0.51 per share. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained in ‘bullish’ territory. Penguin Solutions stock extended its rally, reaching an all-time high of $89.86 on Thursday after delivering better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter (Q3) results and raising its full-year outlook. The rally highlights growing investor confidence in Penguin's expanding role in enterprise artificial intelligence infrastructure, as demand for high-performance computing and memory solutions remains strong. Penguin Solutions posted its strongest-ever Q3 results, with revenue rising 48% year-on-year to $479 million and earnings of $0.84 per share, exceeding the analysts’ consensus estimates of $421 million and $0.56 per share, respectively, according to Fiscal AI data. Several Wall Street firms responded by increasing their price targets following the earnings release. On Wednesday, Barclays analyst Tom O'Malley increased his price target for Penguin Solutions to $40 from $27 while maintaining an ‘Equal Weight’ rating on the stock. Retail sentiment around the stock turned to ‘bullish’ from ‘extremely bullish’ territory the previous day. UnitedHealth stock advanced to a 52-week high of $434.3 on Thursday, ahead of the company's scheduled July 16 fiscal Q2 earnings release. RBC lifted its price target on UNH to $463 from $400 while maintaining its ‘Outperform’ rating, citing favorable trends in the managed care industry. RBC expects health insurers to continue benefiting from the positive momentum seen since April, even as investors remain cautious about medical procedure volumes and patient acuity during the second half of the year. The firm believes the industry's underlying fundamentals remain supportive heading into the upcoming earnings season. On Thursday, UnitedHealthcare launched a Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA), a workplace benefit that allows employers to provide employees with funds for personal health and wellness needs. Retail sentiment around the stock changed to ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish’ territory the previous day. (HIMS) logged their third straight session in the red on Thursday after BofA Securities warned that potential churn among oral Wegovy users could make the company’s expected second-half earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) ramp harder to achieve. HIMS stock slid 2% on Thursday to close at $35.45, with shares also down 4% so far this week. BofA raised its price target on HIMS to $37 from $36, implying a 4% upside from current levels, while keeping a 'Neutral' rating. The brokerage firm said that emerging signs suggest retention of new oral Wegovy members could be “softer than some expect,” supporting BofA’s view that Hims’ implied second-half EBITDA ramp will be “difficult to achieve.” Hims launched oral Wegovy in April and initially saw a strong response. But BofA cited BSM credit and debit card data showing that customers were relatively flat month over month in June. The concern is what happens after the introductory period ends. BofA warned that a meaningful subset of patients could churn once the subscription fee rises from $39 in month one to $149 in month two. BofA pointed to Ro as a warning sign. Ro launched oral Wegovy two to three months before Hims and is already seeing a decline in new customers and a plateauing base, according to the firm. BofA said Hims is “highly likely” to follow a similar path, with some users dropping off after promotional pricing ends. The churn warning comes just months after Hims reset its weight-loss strategy around branded GLP-1 drugs. In March, Hims announced a new agreement with Novo Nordisk to offer FDA-approved branded GLP-1 drugs, including Wegovy and Ozempic, while ending advertising for compounded GLP-1 offerings and helping eligible compounded-GLP-1 patients transition to branded options. By late March, branded Wegovy pills and injections became available through Hims for eligible customers, with cash-pay access starting around $149 per month, plus a separate care membership fee. Hims is also positioning for potential upside from peptides, a wellness category related to weight loss, recovery, joint pain, cognitive performance and longevity. Ahead of a July 23-24 advisory committee meeting, FDA staff said last week that there was insufficient evidence to support allowing compounders to manufacture BPC-157, Emideltide, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax, and TB-500, adding that safety concerns could not be ruled out. This creates a regulatory overhang, but Hims has already moved early. In 2025, the company acquired a California-based peptide manufacturing facility to boost its domestic supply chain and support future work in preventive health, metabolic optimization and recovery science. Needham analyst Ryan MacDonald said the FDA staff view was “a bit of a surprise,” but “not the end of the conversation,” adding that he is still “operating under the assumption that they will get approved.” On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for HIMS slipped to ‘bearish’ levels over the past week, down from ‘neutral’ a month ago, amid a 28% decline in 24-hour message volume. Boeing is reportedly nearing a key FAA certification milestone for its smallest 737 MAX variant, the 737 Max 7, after years of delays that have disrupted airline fleet plans and slowed the company’s commercial recovery. BA shares edged up by about 0.5% after-hours on Thursday. The MAX 7 is expected to receive Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) approval later this month, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Southwest Airlines, with hundreds of orders for the jet, is expected to be the launch customer. An FAA spokesperson told WSJ that the safety approvals would dictate the timing of the MAX 7 certification. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg had predicted earlier this year that the jet would be approved by the end of 2026. The shorter, lighter MAX 7 is designed for shorter routes and offers better fuel efficiency than the older 737-700 it replaces. Together with the larger MAX 10, which competes directly with Airbus’s A321neo family, the two variants complete Boeing’s narrowbody lineup and represent a substantial portion of its undelivered backlog. Delays in the jet’s approval were caused by the 2018-2019 MAX grounding after two fatal crashes, the 2024 Alaska Airlines door-plug incident, and a long-running problem with the engine anti-ice system. Boeing only completed the anti-ice redesign in late 2025. The 737 MAX family is the core of Boeing’s commercial airplanes division and its main source of revenue and orders. Prolonged delays have limited deliveries, slowed cash flow, frustrated major customers, and allowed Airbus to gain ground in the single-aisle market. Since Kelly Ortberg became CEO in August 2024, Boeing has pursued an industrial reset focused on quality and production discipline. The company has strengthened oversight, reacquired fuselage supplier Spirit AeroSystems, and gradually raised output from 38 to 42 aircraft per month, with further increases planned. Certification of the MAX 7 and MAX 10 is viewed as essential to unlocking backlog value and supporting Boeing’s broader recovery. title: UNH, HUM, CNC Stocks Rally On Medicare Advantage Rate Surprise - Stocktwits
content: Shares of insurers UnitedHealth Group (UNH), Centene (CNC), Humana (HUM), and Elevance Health (ELV) jumped in Monday’s extended trading hours after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services announced that the payments to private insurers offering Medicare Advantage plans will increase 2.48% next year. This increase implies $13 billion in additional payments to Medicare insurers for the year, the agency said. “When accounting for estimated risk score trend in MA due to factors such as population changes and coding practices, this amounts to a 4.98% increase,” the agency added. The move came as a surprise since in January, the CMS had proposed a roughly flat increase in payments for private Medicare plans the following year, sending shares of insurers down and wiping out about $100 billion in stock market value. The announcement further comes as a relief to the industry plagued by concerns over rising medical costs. Shares of UNH, CNC, HUM and ELV rallied between 5% and 11% at the time of writing. title: Mural by UNH Grad Unveiled as Part of MUB Dunkin' Redesign - University of New Hampshire
content: Madeline Pender in front of the mural she created for the Dunkin' location in the MUB. The Dunkin’ location inside UNH’s Memorial Union Building (MUB) has a distinct new look, courtesy of a longtime Wildcat. Madeline Pender ’23, ’24G was on hand Oct. 1 to unveil the massive mural she painted as part of Dunkin’s recent redesign in the MUB, a colorful scene full of iconic campus sights and creatively placed Easter eggs – including an image of Pender herself donning a grad cap and gown. Pender’s Wildcat connections run deep. She completed both her undergraduate and graduate degrees at UNH and, after teaching art classes at a nearby high school for a stint, recently returned as an adjunct professor teaching introductory drawing. The mural extends the length of the store and features a host of noteworthy campus landmarks, highlighted by a prominently placed Wildcat statue and an image of Thompson Hall. It also includes several nods to Dunkin’, including students holding the chain’s distinctive beverage cups. “We started to look at moments most UNH students could see themselves in, whether that was sitting on T-Hall lawn together, going to a hockey game, looking for some more iconic moments,” Pender says. Pender included a diverse array of students, including figures in scrubs or a lab coat, to “get a nod” to each of UNH’s colleges in the image. She also included some Easter eggs, like a depiction of her friend, Eli Bryant ’24, painting UNH’s DriX uncrewed surface vessel, which can map the seafloor autonomously, as well as her own cameo. “I had to have a little ‘Where’s Waldo’ moment, kind of a fun nod to my time here,” Pender says. Dunkin’ hired Pender to conceive and paint the mural as part of a redesign that will inaugurate the UNH location as a Dunkin’ “Signature Series” store, according to a Boston Globe story, a distinction highlighted by branding and design elements created to reflect the local community. Dunkin’ noted that the MUB location is the first such store on a college campus in New England. "Wildcats have always run on Dunkin'. My team and I love serving this community and being a part of students' daily lives, from their first stop in the morning to fueling their late nights studying," says Durval Salema, store owner and Dunkin' franchisee. "We are deeply proud to be the first Dunkin' Signature Series store at a college or university in New England. The new mural beautifully marks that milestone and captures Dunkin’s partnership with UNH. Every time students, faculty, or staff stop in, they'll be reminded of the people, campus, moments, and traditions that make the campus community special." Pender told the Globe that she partnered with Dunkin’ and representatives from UNH to work through several potential designs for the mural. She hand-painted the final scene, broken into different elements, which were digitally assembled and printed onto a wall covering. “I feel super lucky,” Pender told the Globe. “I don’t think I ever would have anticipated that I’d be in this position, not only to work with such a fun and well-known company, but also to be in such a public space where I have this lasting imprint. … I feel like it summarizes my time at UNH very well.” Copyright © 2026 , University of New Hampshire. title: UNH police report car and scooter thefts, advise security - Seacoastonline.com
content: DURHAM — Campus police at the University of New Hampshire are reporting recent motor vehicle and electric scooter thefts. Two stolen scooter reports were made Monday, Oct. 5 to UNH police, following the recovery of a motor vehicle that was taken in late September. The car, a gray Chevrolet Trax, was stolen on campus between Sept. 27 at 6 p.m. and Sept. 28 at 2 p.m., according to UNH police. The keys were in the vehicle, which was then recovered in another municipality. Police at UNH did not immediately disclose where the car was located, nor whether charges have been filed in connection with the incident. The two scooters have yet to be found, police stated Oct. 6. The first, a black Leqismart scooter with a “Mega Wheels” sticker on its stem, was taken from the bike rack outside Philbrook Hall at 2:30 p.m. Oct. 5. The second stolen scooter, a black Hi-Boy KS4, was removed from the rack outside Jessie Doe Hall between 1 and 5 p.m. the same day, per UNH police. University police released an emergency bulletin about the thefts on Tuesday, Oct. 6. Police advised students and community members to keep their keys on hand and lock their vehicles, in addition to securing scooters with locks and leaving identifying tags or markers on them. Police encouraged scooter owners to register their scooters with the university. All three thefts remain under investigation. Members of the public with information about the incidents are asked to contact UNH police at (603) 862-1427.

title: UnitedHealth Q3 Coming Up: Two Questions Investors Can't Ignore - TradingView
content: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated UNH heads into third-quarter earnings on Oct. 13 with a different test than it faced earlier this year. The focus is no longer simply on whether results are improving. Investors now want to know whether the second-quarter rebound can hold. UnitedHealthcare’s MCR improved to 86.7% in the second quarter from 89.4% a year earlier. Operating earnings rose to $3.9 billion from $2.1 billion, while operating margin climbed to 4.6% from 2.4%. Still, the quarter included $860 million of favorable medical reserve development, which helped the reported improvement. That leaves investors looking for cleaner evidence in the third quarter. Key areas include underlying medical costs, Medicare inpatient and outpatient utilization, commercial cost trends, specialty-drug inflation and provider coding intensity. Management’s 88.1% full-year MCR outlook will also be closely watched. The second major question is whether UnitedHealthcare can repair Medicare Advantage profitability without giving up too much enrollment. MA membership stood at 7.565 million at June 30, down 785,000 from a year earlier. Including certain complex populations, senior enrollment had fallen by about 965,000 since 2025-end. Management expects the full-year MA decline to reach roughly 1.1 million members. Some of that pressure is intentional. UNH has been adjusting benefits, pricing, networks and market exposure to improve returns. Management still expects Medicare margins to finish 2026 above 3%. The third quarter will show whether the trade-off is working. Investors will be watching enrollment, retention, benefit changes for 2027 and any update to the attrition forecast. A smaller, healthier Medicare book could support earnings, but deeper membership losses would raise fresh concerns about growth. The strongest outcome would pair steadier medical costs with improving Medicare economics and member retention. Peers like Humana Inc. HUM and Elevance Health, Inc. ELV are also fighting rising medical cost trends. Neither Humana nor Elevance Health showed year-over-year cost-ratio improvement in the last reported quarter. Humana’s Insurance benefit ratio rose to 91.2% from 89.9%, up 130 basis points, despite some inpatient favorability. Elevance’s benefit expense ratio increased to 89.7% from 88.9%, up 80 basis points, mainly reflecting elevated medical costs in its Government businesses, partly offset by better ACA performance. title: At UNH Forum, Shaheen Shifts Left on Energy, Hits DiLorenzo Over Natural Gas - NH Journal
content: Stefany Shaheen’s transformation from establishment Democrat to progressive activist continued at a University of New Hampshire forum Monday evening as she moved left on energy policy. Her position puts Shaheen, daughter of establishment icon U.S. Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, to the left of many in her party who are moving toward an “all-of-the-above” energy policy as consumer costs rise. Asked about energy policy by Kevin Sullivan, a UNH alumnus and associate editor of The Washington Post, Shaheen threw her support behind green energy technology and the billions in subsidies the Biden administration poured into it. “We’ve got to restore the tax incentives that were cut from the disastrous budget bill that was passed last year that cut incentives for wind and solar,” Shaheen said. “Not only did they cut the incentives, but they are now taxing wind and solar.” (A proposed excise tax on wind and solar was removed from the “One Big Beautiful Bill.” There is no specific federal tax on wind or solar energy.) Shaheen also went out of her way to hit her GOP opponent, Anthony DiLorenzo, over his support for expanding natural gas pipelines into New England. “He’s talking about building a gas pipeline. I’ve heard him talk about fracking,” Shaheen said. “None of that’s going to help the man I talked to on Saturday help his parents afford their heating oil.” That’s a shift for Shaheen, who was on WMUR during the early days of the NH-01 campaign supporting pipelines and other fossil fuel options. When WMUR’s Adam Sexton asked whether she would support a new pipeline bringing natural gas to New Hampshire, Shaheen said she supported “keeping all options on the table,” including the pipeline. “Ultimately, I think electricity costs and energy costs are way too high in New Hampshire, and we have to keep all options on the table,” Shaheen said. “I’d need to better understand where the pipeline was coming from and what kind of disruption it would cause, but I think we need to be open to all options that would address climate challenges and energy costs.” During the same forum, DiLorenzo reiterated his support for cheap natural gas from Pennsylvania to lower costs for Granite Staters. “Pennsylvania is the Saudi Arabia of natural gas. It’s the cleanest-burning fossil fuel there is,” DiLorenzo said. One of his first priorities in Congress would be to build support for lowering the barriers blue states like Massachusetts and New York have put up to block pipelines to northern New England. “I’ve already talked to Secretary of Energy (Chris) Wright about it. I’ve talked to two congresspeople from Pennsylvania about it, and I’m starting to build a coalition of people that will help me with that initiative of bringing a pipeline in.” Wright was in New Hampshire in August, when he made the point that the lack of access to energy is putting New England at risk of blackouts during harsh winter weather. At peak demand during a storm in January 2026, Wright said that only 2% of the state’s electricity supply came from wind, solar, and batteries combined. Another 3% came from burning trash and wood, with 9% being hydropower imported from Canada. “The biggest source of electrical generation at that time was burning oil because there’s not enough gas pipelines in New England,” Wright said. “When it gets cold, gas gets diverted to heat homes, and there’s not enough for the power plants.” Wright’s remarks were echoed by DiLorenzo, who also reiterated his support for a natural gas pipeline from Pennsylvania to New Hampshire. “We don’t have access to natural gas via a pipeline because our neighboring states, Massachusetts and New York, won’t let us have that,” DiLorenzo said. “That would significantly reduce our energy costs and bring a significant supply of energy.” Leonard Robinson writes about politics and finance for InsideSources. title: Aspire Acquires Former UNH Orange Campus for New Center - Orange Town News
content: Aspire Living & Learning, a nonprofit serving neurodivergent children and adults, today announced it has purchased the former University of New Haven satellite campus at 584 Derby Milford Road in Orange.Buy Maps The campus will become the new home of the Trumbull location of Aspire Living & Learning Academy (ALL Academy), Aspire’s private special  education school, as well as its adult community-based day program and Connecticut administrative offices currently based in Hamden. ALL Academy’s Naugatuck and Stamford locations will remain where they are. Aspire closed on the 47-acre property September 28th. The campus includes a 70,680-square-foot building, which Aspire will renovate over the coming year to create dedicated environments for each program. Programming is expected to begin in summer 2027. “We’ve been looking for an opportunity like this in Connecticut,” said Erica Hare, Aspire CEO. “Orange gives us room to strengthen what we offer today while also thinking about where we want to go next. We can create spaces that better support the work happening now while giving Aspire room to grow and respond to what the people we support and communities around us need in the years ahead.”Tour Colleges For ALL Academy, the move is an opportunity to raise the bar for what a special education school can offer. Aspire’s plans for Orange will prioritize accessibility and innovation while creating an environment where students have access to the learning, technology, experiences and opportunities they deserve, without having to choose between individualized support and a rich school experience. “Special education shouldn’t be about fitting a student into a program. It should be about building the right environment around that student,” said Dr. Elizabeth Sellinger, chief of clinical and children’s services. “Orange gives us an opportunity to push that thinking further, to be innovative in how students learn and build skills, and to create more pathways for each student to work toward the future they want.” That same focus on access and independence will extend beyond the school. Aspire’s adult community-based day program will have dedicated space at Orange while continuing to use the surrounding community as an important part of the program. For students and adults alike, the campus will be a starting point for learning, work, skill-building and experiences that extend well beyond it.Read Newspapers Aspire plans to continue building relationships with employers, businesses and community organizations throughout the area to expand opportunities for employment, internships, volunteering and community-based learning. Volunteers and donors will also have opportunities to contribute, with philanthropic support helping fund technology, equipment, additional environments and experiences beyond the core renovation. “There are so many ways to be part of what we’re creating in Orange,” said John Whittemore, associate vice president of growth and advancement at Aspire. “For some, that might mean becoming an employment partner or volunteering their time and expertise. For others, it might mean making a gift that helps bring an idea for the campus to life. Each can open up new opportunities for the people we support.” Aspire will share renovation updates, additional plans for the campus and opportunities to visit, partner and get involved throughout the coming year. title: UNH Exits Select Medicare Advantage Plans for 2027 Amid Cost Pressure - The Globe and Mail
content: UnitedHealth Group Incorporated UNH is scaling back parts of its Medicare Advantage (MA) business for 2027 as elevated medical costs and utilization continue to pressure profitability. Per Bloomberg, UnitedHealthcare will discontinue plans covering about 390,000 members next year. The move reflects a more selective approach as the insurer focuses on improving the economics of its Medicare business. The retrenchment is part of a broader industry reset, with insurers placing greater emphasis on plan-level profitability rather than maximizing enrollment. Reuters reported that UnitedHealthcare plans to exit locations where it has a higher concentration of preferred provider organization (PPO) plans, which offer broader out-of-network access but can carry higher costs. For UNH, reducing exposure to less profitable plans could strengthen returns in Medicare Advantage as medical cost trends remain elevated. Beyond portfolio changes, UNH plans to invest nearly $1.5 billion in AI-related initiatives in 2026, aiming to improve productivity and reduce administrative burden. The company is also shifting toward narrower-network offerings. UnitedHealthcare said that 66% of members will have access to both health maintenance organization (HMO) and PPO plans in 2027, compared with 70% in 2026, according to Reuters. Still, the strategy comes with a membership trade-off, as some displaced members could move to competitors instead of remaining within UnitedHealthcare. However, prioritizing sustainable margins over membership growth could support UNH’s earnings recovery. With the MA market facing persistent cost and reimbursement challenges, tighter plan selection could help the company build a healthier membership mix and improve Medicare Advantage profitability while preserving exposure to the market’s long-term growth opportunity. Some of UNH’s major competitors in the healthcare service provider space are Humana Inc.HUM and Centene CorporationCNC. Humana is also pruning its Medicare Advantage portfolio for 2027, with exits expected to affect roughly 600,000 members. The insurer is prioritizing stronger-performing plans and value-based care exposure, aiming to protect profitability while redirecting affected members toward other HUM plans. Centene is taking a selective approach to Medicare Advantage for 2027. Per Becker’s Payer Issues, CNC’s Wellcare is reducing its plan lineup and exiting Hawaii, Oklahoma and Tennessee, while retaining Special Needs Plans in Nevada and Ohio as it refines strategy. Shares of UNH have gained 32.2% over the past six months compared with the industry’s rise of 32.1%. From a valuation standpoint, UnitedHealth trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 16.98, above the industry average of 14.93. UNH carries a Value Score of B. title: Paul and Grayce Anderson Honored With Hubbard Award at Evening of Distinction - University of New Hampshire
content: UNH recognized Paul and Grayce Anderson with the Hubbard Family Award for Service to Philanthropy at the university’s annual Evening of Distinction celebration Oct. 1. The event is UNH’s signature celebration of alumni and the impact of philanthropy. The Hubbard Award is UNH’s “highest honor bestowed upon those whose philanthropic leadership has significantly strengthened the state of New Hampshire, its communities, and the university.” It was established in 2001 to honor Oliver, Austin, and Leslie Hubbard. UNH is where the story began for Paul and Grayce Anderson, who met during their time as students on campus. They both went on to successful and fulfilling careers in the field of chemistry and have continued their UNH story with transformational support for the university’s chemistry department, support that has and will make a real and lasting impact for generations of students and faculty. Paul and Grayce Anderson at Evening of Distinction. Between their philanthropy to date, which has helped advance high-priority research and faculty excellence in chemistry at UNH, and a legacy gift of nearly half their amassed wealth to be bestowed upon the chemistry department, the Andersons are among the top 10 most generous benefactors in UNH history. Support from the Andersons helped fund the university’s first endowed professorship in the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences — the Gloria G. and Dr. Robert E. Lyle Professorship, named in honor of Paul’s beloved faculty mentor, Robert Lyle, and his wife, Gloria. Paul credits Lyle’s guidance and mentorship as a big part of his inspiration to pursue what would become a lifetime career in medicinal chemistry. That career saw Paul spend time at Merck Sharp & Dohme Research Laboratories, DuPont Pharmaceuticals, and Bristol-Myers Squibb, helping direct several groundbreaking drug discovery efforts. He spent time as vice president of chemistry at Merck and later as senior vice president for chemical and physical sciences at DuPont, and earned numerous awards throughout his career, including the Priestley Medal, the highest honor granted by the American Chemical Society (ACS). Grayce spent her professional career as a chemist with Pfizer. She was something of a trailblazer in the field of chemistry at a time when few women were breaking through in the industry, and she stepped away after a handful of years to care for aging parents and to support Paul as he ascended to influential leadership roles. UNH has a rich history of pioneering success in chemistry — our own Conant Hall was designated by the American Chemical Society as its first National Historic Chemical Landmark in New England — and the Andersons have positioned the department to carry that strength through the present and well into the future thanks to their vision and generosity. They have left an unmistakably powerful imprint on UNH. Copyright © 2026 , University of New Hampshire. All rights reserved.

Earlier, it sold karaoke machines and audio equipment. The SemiCab business achieved an annualized run rate of $10 million last year, thanks to five new contract wins with some of the largest multinational fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies in India and six contract expansions, the company said in its results statement. In the new year, it has added Coca-Cola India and MTR Foods as new clients. (TSLA) flashed fresh warning signals on Monday after slipping below key levels following a first-quarter (Q1) delivery miss, with one analyst projecting nearly 40% downside by June as bearish calls built after JPMorgan flagged a major downside to the stock. TSLA stock fell more than 2% on Monday, marking its lowest level in nearly seven months. GLJ Research analyst Gordon Johnson said on X that Tesla has broken below its 20, 50 and 75-day moving averages and remains trapped in a descending channel that began after the stock’s December highs near $480. He added that Fibonacci levels point to $322 as the next key support, while momentum indicators indicate the stock is not yet oversold. Johnson said investors should watch the $322- $346 range for a potential bounce. The analyst also said that, assuming consensus expectations for negative $1.6 billion in first-quarter free cash flow prove accurate and that prior correlations between Tesla’s free cash flow performance and its share price continue to hold, the stock could fall to $224-$269 by June 30, implying a 24%-36% downside from current levels. He also noted that Tesla’s car sales declined year-over-year in both 2024 and 2025 and are expected to fall again in 2026. “$TSLA has made literally NO PROGRESS on ‘robotaxis’ since launching in Austin in June of last yr. It could fall another 70-80%, and STILL be massively overvalued,” Johnson said, adding that the stock trades as 288x estimated 2026 earnings versus 31x for the Magnificent Seven. Johnson’s technical warning follows a bearish update from JPMorgan analyst Ryan Brinkman, who reiterated an ‘Underweight’ rating and set a $145 price target after Tesla’s Q1 delivery report, implying a 60% downside to current levels. “We ... advise investors approach TSLA shares with a high degree of caution,” Brinkman said. He also lowered 2026 earnings per share (EPS) estimate to $1.8 from $2, below consensus expectations, citing risks to demand, execution and competition as Tesla expands into lower-priced, higher-volume vehicle segments. Future Fund Managing Partner Gary Black said on X, “TSLA bulls out in full force today attacking Ryan Brinkman the person. Yes he’s been wrong on TSLA for 10 years, but he’s been right on TSLA the past five years, so has some credibility.” Separately, Jim Cramer called the bearish JPMorgan call “bold” and speculated that it “must mean people are going to sell this one to buy SpaceX.” His comment follows reports that SpaceX has confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering that could become the largest IPO on record, with the company reportedly valued at about $1.75 trillion. Tesla delivered 358,023 vehicles globally in the first quarter, missing Wall Street expectations for a second straight quarter. Deliveries rose 6% from the previous year but fell 14% from a quarter ago, marking the company’s weakest quarter since 2022 outside a Model Y production adjustment period. The company produced 408,386 vehicles during the quarter. Model 3 and Model Y deliveries totaled 341,893 units, while Model S, Model X and Cybertruck deliveries reached 16,130 units. Tesla also deployed 8.8 gigawatt-hours of energy-storage products, down from 10.4 gigawatt-hours a year earlier and below estimates. The results come as the U.S. electric-vehicle market adjusts to the phase-out of federal purchase incentives and competition from Chinese automakers intensifies across markets. Even as bearish calls emerged after the delivery miss, Baird maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating and lowered its price target to $538 from $548, still implying a 52% upside from the stock’s last close, according to an Investing report. Meanwhile, Canaccord Genuity reiterated a ‘Buy’ rating and maintained its $420 price target, representing a 19% upside from current levels following the delivery update. The brokerage noted that rising gasoline prices and firmer domestic used-Tesla pricing could support future demand. Shares of insurers UnitedHealth Group (UNH), Centene (CNC), Humana (HUM), and Elevance Health (ELV) jumped in Monday’s extended trading hours after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services announced that the payments to private insurers offering Medicare Advantage plans will increase 2.48% next year. This increase implies $13 billion in additional payments to Medicare insurers for the year, the agency said. “When accounting for estimated risk score trend in MA due to factors such as population changes and coding practices, this amounts to a 4.98% increase,” the agency added. The move came as a surprise since in January, the CMS had proposed a roughly flat increase in payments for private Medicare plans the following year, sending shares of insurers down and wiping out about $100 billion in stock market value. The announcement further comes as a relief to the industry plagued by concerns over rising medical costs. Shares of UNH, CNC, HUM and ELV rallied between 5% and 11% at the time of writing. Shares of Aetna parent CVS Health (CVS) rose by about 6.5% while Molina Healthcare (MOH) stock rose a modest 3%. While UnitedHealth is the largest provider of private Medicare Advantage plans in the U.S., Humana is the second largest. Sentiment around HUM stock, meanwhile, increased from ‘neutral’ to ‘extremely bullish’ territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume rose from ‘normal’ to ‘extremely high’ levels.
